nodes.summary: The convex sub-Gaussian comparison constant, the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of all admissible variance factors, equals $c_0^2$, where $c_0$ is the Davis–Power constant.
nodes.title: Davis–Power value of the convex sub-Gaussian comparison constant

nodes.summary: The comparison constant is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the set of admissible comparison constants $C$; it equals $\infty$ when no admissible constant exists.
nodes.title: The convex sub-Gaussian comparison constant

nodes.summary: Let $A = \int_0^\infty \min(1, 2e^{-t^2/2})\,dt$, the integral over $[0, \infty)$ of the capped Gaussian tail envelope $t \mapsto \min(1, 2e^{-t^2/2})$.

nodes.summary: Let $B = A/2$, where $A = \int_0^\infty \min(1, 2e^{-t^2/2})\,dt$ is the integral over $[0, \infty)$ of the capped Gaussian tail envelope.
nodes.title: Half the envelope integral, $B$

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi(t) = e^{-t^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ be the standard Gaussian density, $B = \frac12 \int_0^\infty \min(1, 2e^{-t^2/2})\,dt$ and $h(x) = 2x e^{-x^2/2} + 2\int_x^\infty e^{-t^2/2}\,dt$. This is the set of reals $c_0$ for which there are reals $a$, $p_0$, $z$ with $a > \sqrt{2 \log 2}$, $h(a) = B$, $p_0 = 2e^{-a^2/2}$, $0 < p_0 < 1$, $\int_z^\infty \varphi(t)\,dt = p_0$ and $c_0 = B / \varphi(z)$.
nodes.title: Values of $c_0$ solving the Davis–Power system

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi(t) = e^{-t^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ be the standard Gaussian density, $B = \frac12 \int_0^\infty \min(1, 2e^{-t^2/2})\,dt$ and $h(x) = 2x e^{-x^2/2} + 2\int_x^\infty e^{-t^2/2}\,dt$. nodes.summary: A parameter quadruple is a quadruple $(a, p_0, z, c_0)$ of real numbers, the unknowns of the Davis–Power equation system. Being a solution of the system is a separate condition.
nodes.title: Parameter quadruples of the Davis–Power system

nodes.summary: There is exactly one quadruple $(a, p_0, z, c_0)$ of real numbers that is a valid solution of the Davis–Power system.
nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness for the Davis–Power system

nodes.summary: The transition threshold is the real number $t_0 = \sqrt{2\log 2}$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: The Davis–Power transition threshold

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an admissible comparison constant, let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ have a 1-sub-Gaussian tail. Then $X$ is convexly dominated by $\sqrt{C}\,G$, where $G$ is a standard Gaussian random variable (the identity on $\mathbb{R}$ under the standard normal law $N(0, 1)$).
nodes.title: Admissible constants compare variables on every sample space

nodes.summary: For a real number $t$, the capped Gaussian tail envelope at $t$ is $\min\{1, 2 e^{-t^2/2}\}$.
nodes.title: The capped Gaussian tail envelope

nodes.summary: The comparison constant is finite. nodes.title: Finiteness of the convex sub-Gaussian comparison constant

nodes.summary: An extended nonnegative real $C \in [0, \infty]$ is an admissible comparison constant when $0 < C < \infty$ and, for every probability measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $\Omega$ and every function $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ with a 1-sub-Gaussian tail under $\mu$, $X$ under $\mu$ is convexly dominated by the function $g \mapsto \sqrt{C}\, g$ under the standard Gaussian measure $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Admissible convex sub-Gaussian comparison constants

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$. A function $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ has a 1-sub-Gaussian tail when it is measurable and integrable, has mean $\int X \, d\mu = 0$, and satisfies $\mu\{\omega : |X(\omega)| > t\} \le 2 e^{-t^2/2}$ for every real $t \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Random variables with a 1-sub-Gaussian tail

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi(t) = e^{-t^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ be the standard Gaussian density, $Q(x) = \int_x^\infty \varphi(t)\,dt$ its upper tail, $t_0 = \sqrt{2\log 2}$ with $\log$ the natural logarithm, $B = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^\infty \min(1, 2e^{-t^2/2})\,dt$ and $h(x) = 2x e^{-x^2/2} + 2\int_x^\infty e^{-t^2/2}\,dt$. A quadruple $(a, p_0, z, c_0)$ of real numbers is a valid solution of the Davis–Power system when $a > t_0$,…
nodes.title: Valid solutions of the Davis–Power system

nodes.summary: The convex sub-Gaussian comparison constant is at least $1$. This holds also when no admissible comparison constant exists, in which case the constant is $\infty$.
nodes.title: The comparison constant is at least one

nodes.summary: Every admissible comparison constant $C$ satisfies $C \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Admissible comparison constants are at least one

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$. A function $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ saturates the Gaussian tail when $\mu\{\omega : |X(\omega)| > t\} = \min\{1, 2 e^{-t^2/2}\}$ for every real $t \ge 0$, that is, its strict tails equal the capped Gaussian tail envelope.
nodes.title: Saturating the Gaussian tail envelope

nodes.summary: For a real number $x$, the standard Gaussian upper tail at $x$ is $Q(x) = \int_x^\infty \varphi(t)\,dt$, where $\varphi(t) = e^{-t^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ is the standard Gaussian density.
nodes.title: Standard Gaussian upper tail

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
